name: door styles
_about: THE DOORS OF THE WORLD'S BUILDERS, by tradition: what a building's doors file (assets/doors/<building>.json) names as its `style` -- a look (doors.js: boards, iron, trellis, panel, bronze, studded, lattice, carved, plain), its colours (`color` the wood, lacquer or metal; `accent` the iron, gilt, brass or paper) and its leaves. An entry in a building's file says anything over its style.

gothic._about: oak under wrought-iron scrolls: a Gothic portal's (Notre-Dame's Biscornet ironwork)

gothic-great._about: a cathedral's great portal: its leaves stand shut, the wicket cut in one of them is the way in

romanesque._about: plainer oak, fewer straps: an abbey's

tower._about: a stair turret's or a tower's small door: planks on battens, strap hinges

bronze._about: cast bronze in coffers, a boss in each: the Pantheon's, Pisa's, Milan's, St Isaac's

bronze-great._about: a great bronze portal, shut, a wicket in it

greek._about: a temple's cella doors: wood sheathed in bronze, studded with bosses

baroque._about: a baroque church's or palace's: stiles, rails and raised panels, a brass handle

baroque-green._about: painted green, as Viennese and Saxon doors often are

classical._about: a Georgian or neoclassical door: dark oak in panels

palace._about: a palace's inner doors: painted pale, the mouldings gilt

castle._about: a castle gate: heavy oak, iron, a wicket

russian._about: a Russian church's: painted boards under a lattice of iron straps

byzantine._about: bronze-sheathed oak, as Hagia Sophia's and St Mark's

islamic._about: a mosque's: walnut carved in lozenges, brass bosses and a knocker

ottoman._about: inlaid with mother-of-pearl: the Ottoman mosques'

persian._about: silver-plated over the carving: the Shah's mosque in Isfahan

mughal._about: a Mughal tomb's: dark wood, brass

gulf._about: teak with gilded brass: the new mosques of the Gulf

chinese-gate._about: an imperial gate: vermilion lacquer, nine rows of gilt nail heads, a lion's-head ring

chinese-hall._about: a hall's geshan doors: red lattice over paper, a solid panel below

japanese-swing._about: a temple's itatobira: vermilion boards on battens studded with gilt nail heads

japanese-slide._about: sliding doors of wood and paper

japanese-castle._about: a castle gate: dark wood under iron plates and straps

egyptian._about: cedar of Lebanon, bound in gilt bronze: a temple's

french._about: a French door: glazed above a low panel, painted pale (Versailles's, a baroque palace's garden doors)
